faq.q: Why is a raisin so sugary inside?
faq.a: A raisin is a grape that has lost most of its water by drying in the sun. The sugar stays behind, so the cells end up very concentrated.
asks: Tell me about the sugary raisin

faq.q: What is a partially permeable membrane?
faq.a: It is a thin layer with tiny gaps that let small molecules like water pass through but stop bigger ones like sugar. Cell membranes work like this.
asks: Tell me about the skin filter

faq.a: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a partially permeable membrane, from a dilute solution, with lots of water, to a more concentrated solution, with less water.
asks: Tell me about water moving in

faq.q: Why does salt make vegetables go floppy?
faq.a: Salty water outside is more concentrated than the cell sap inside, so water leaves the cells by osmosis. The cells go soft and the vegetable flops.
asks: Why do cucumbers go soft in salt?

faq.q: Is osmosis a kind of diffusion?
faq.a: Yes. Osmosis is a special case of diffusion: it is only about water moving across a partially permeable membrane.
asks: How is osmosis different from diffusion?

facts: Osmosis is the net movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from a dilute to a more concentrated solution.
Plant cells placed in very salty water lose water by osmosis and become soft, or flaccid.

quiz.say: A raisin is put in pure water. Which way does water move?
quiz.show: A raisin is put in pure water. Which way does water move?
quiz.why: The raisin is more concentrated than pure water, so water moves into it by osmosis.

wrong.0: Water moves out only when the outside is more concentrated, like salty water.
wrong.2: There is a big concentration difference, so water does move.
